papers.title: Enhancing cortical electrophysiological signatures of sleep overrides ER stress responses in sleep-deprived mice
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) triggers characteristic changes in the cortical electroencephalogram (EEG) during waking and sleep, as well as upregulating molecular signatures of neuronal activity, synaptic plasticity, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. This includes the induction of the unfolded protein response (UPR), the primary marker and adaptive mechanism of ER stress. Yet how cortical neuronal activity during SD contributes to the induction of these molecular signatures remains unknown. Here we investigate whether manipulating cortical activity during SD with a physiological stimulation paradigm (flickering light stimulation, FLS) affects the induction of the UPR. As expected, SD alone upregulated activity-dependent and UPR-related genes in cortex and led to increased EEG slow-wave activity (SWA) during subsequent NREM sleep, an electrophysiological signature of sleep need. Delivering FLS during SD, however, prevented the upregulation of activity- and UPR-related genes while inducing an additional increase in SWA during subsequent sleep. Further analysis of neuronal firing revealed that FLS induced brief neuronal silent (OFF) periods in awake animals during stimulation, thereby shifting cortical activity towards a brain state resembling sleep. These findings suggest that physiological manipulation of cortical activity during waking is sufficient to dissociate molecular signatures of ER stress from electrophysiological markers of sleep pressure. We propose that global sleep wake history and cortical network dynamics differentially regulate activity-dependent transcription and the accumulation of sleep pressure.

papers.title: REM Sleep Iota Oscillations Across the Lifespan
papers.abstract: Iota oscillations are a newly discovered marker of wakefulness and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. So far, iota in REM sleep has only been reported in the surface electroencephalography (EEG) of a small sample of young adults and in intracranial recordings of epileptic patients. Here, we investigated the presence of these oscillations in a large dataset (N=937) of high-density sleep EEG recordings from individuals 7 to 70 years old. We found that iota spectral peaks during REM sleep were between 25 and 40 Hz, slightly faster than in wake (25-35 Hz). Iota power was significantly associated with REM sleep architecture, increasing with both REM duration and across progressive sleep cycles. Iota peaks were observed in individuals of all ages, although the prevalence decreased gradually with age, from 88% in children to 44% in older adults. Most iota spectral peak properties (frequency, amplitude, timing, topography) likewise shifted with age. The most striking effect, however, was in bandwidth, such that children had narrow iota peaks, older adults had broad iota peaks, and 20-30 year olds could have either. It remains unclear whether narrowband and broadband iota are functionally equivalent. On shorter time scales (< 1 year), iota properties remained stable across measurements. Analyses of a separate dataset of monozygotic and dizygotic twins revealed high heritability of all iota peak properties except bandwidth. Overall, these results establish iota as a genetically determined trait-like marker of REM sleep with unique age-related changes. Iota oscillations open new avenues to investigate the interaction between sleep, genetics, development, and aging.

Twin analyses indicated high heritability of most iota peak properties except bandwidth, supporting iota as a genetically determined, trait-like REM sleep marker.

papers.title: NED-Net: an annotation-training loop for rodent EEG event detection
papers.abstract: Long-term EEG monitoring is central to rodent epilepsy research, and manual review is laborious because recordings span hundreds to tens of thousands of animal-hours. Published automated detectors perform well on their development datasets but are typically fixed models that may not adapt to another laboratory's electrodes, animals, or noise conditions. We introduce NED-Net, open-source software for training and maintaining seizure detectors. It uses reviewed candidate events as training labels, runs detection live during recording, and retrains as annotations accumulate. A detector trained on one mouse cohort (867 annotated seizures) achieved 93.6% precision in human review of 171 detections. Applied unchanged to a second cohort on the same acquisition system, its detections were mostly seizures (12 of 13 reviewed), but per-animal recall varied substantially (median 10%), with no convulsive reference seizure detected in four of 11 animals. Retraining with annotations from the second cohort raised convulsive recall from 15% to 64%, with at least one reference seizure detected in every animal. On recordings withheld from training, 75% of detections were seizures and 14 of 22 reference seizures were detected, whereas the source model and a model trained without these animals detected none. NED-Net supports evaluating and adapting detectors to local recordings.

papers.title: Sleep reactivation shapes memories of event and its temporal structure
papers.abstract: Episodic memory provides a temporal scaffold that organizes past experiences according to their sequential occurrence. While memories are reactivated and consolidated during sleep, it remains unknown how exogenous reactivation reshapes memories of complex events, particularly the temporal structure that binds individual elements across time. In this preregistered study, 35 participants encoded neutral and aversive narratives composed of image sequences, with auditory context shifts defining event boundaries. During post-encoding slow-wave sleep, closed-loop targeted memory reactivation (TMR) delivered boundary-associated auditory cues time-locked to the up-state of slow oscillations. Reactivation led to faster, more confident, and more liberal recognition responses for cued than uncued memories. However, reactivation exerted a time-dependent effect on temporal-order memory, impairing it immediately after sleep but attenuating forgetting one week later. This behavioral dissociation was paralleled at the neural level: stronger cue-elicited theta activity predicted superior recognition of neutral, but not aversive event content, whereas greater theta responses were associated with poorer temporal-order memory for the same events. Together, these findings suggest that sleep reactivation does not uniformly strengthen episodic memories. Rather, it selectively prioritizes access to event content while reorganizing temporal relations among event elements, revealing distinct, time-dependent consequences of sleep reactivation for different components of complex experiences.

papers.title: Effect of Long-Term Physical Exercise on Memory, Anxiety-Like Behavior, and Depression in Young and Aged Male Mice Subjected to Sleep Deprivation.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated whether chronic aerobic exercise could attenuate behavioral impairments associated with sleep deprivation (SD) in young and aged male mice. Young (3 months) and aged (18 months) Swiss mice were assigned to four groups: control, exercise (EXE), sleep deprivation (SD), and exercise followed by SD (EXE + SD). Animals performed treadmill training for 8 weeks and then underwent 72-hour SD. Behavioral tests assessed working memory (Y-maze), depression-like behavior (tail suspension), and anxiety-like behavior (elevated plus maze). The results suggest that age influences the effectiveness of exercise in mitigating sleep deprivation-induced behavioral deficits, opening avenues for future studies on the interaction between physical exercise, sleep, and aging.

papers.title: Daytime Napping and Associative-Memory Retrieval Speed: An Exploratory Behavioral and EEG Study
papers.abstract: Purpose: To test whether a daytime nap was associated with improved associative-recognition performance relative to monitored wakefulness and to determine where any response-time (RT) difference occurred in the RT distribution. Methods: Fifteen healthy students completed nap and wake sessions in a within-participant design. Each session included word-pair learning, immediate recognition, a 60-min interval, and delayed recognition without additional study. Trial-level log RT was the focal outcome; accuracy and electroencephalography (EEG) were complementary outcomes. Results: The RT Condition-by-Time interaction was significant (b = -0.063, 95% CI [-0.117, -0.009], p = .027). Responses were 6.7% faster after the nap (p = .010) but did not change after wakefulness (p = .704), with the difference concentrated among slower responses. Accuracy showed no condition-specific change (p = .401). Nap EEG showed aperiodic spectral slowing and stronger periodic sigma activity, but no EEG measure explained the RT effect. Conclusions: Daytime napping was associated with faster delayed associative recognition, primarily through attenuation of the slowest responses. The exploratory findings warrant larger confirmatory studies.

papers.title: Sleep Spindles and Slow Oscillations as Potential Biomarkers and Therapeutic Targets in Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: This review critically evaluates evidence on sleep spindles (SP), slow oscillations (SOs), and their coordination in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease (AD), focusing on their relationships with cognition, AD biomarkers, and their therapeutic potential. Longitudinal studies associate greater SP and/or SO activity with better cognition and favourable amyloid and tau profiles after clinical onset. Spindle and SO coupling may index network integrity. Preserved NREM sleep oscillations are associated with lower orexin concentrations and weaker adverse relationships between orexin and cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes. Closed-loop acoustic stimulation and slow-oscillatory transcranial direct-current stimulation can modify SO activity, spindle activity, and coupling, although cognitive and biomarker benefits remain uncertain. Spindle-SO activity, including their temporal coupling, are associated with cognition and AD biomarkers across the disease continuum. Closed-loop acoustic and electrical stimulation can modify these oscillations, but biomarker-characterized trials in MCI and AD are needed to determine whether treatment produces durable cognitive and biomarker benefits.

papers.title: Portable polysomnography-derived multi-domain EEG markers of anesthetic state transitions during propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy.
papers.abstract: Propofol anesthesia is widely used for gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, but electroencephalographic (EEG) features of anesthetic state transitions in this brief and stimulus-rich setting remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to describe clinically interpretable EEG markers across anesthetic stages using portable polysomnography (PSG)-derived six-channel EEG. In this prospective observational study, 31 adults undergoing GI endoscopy under propofol-based anesthesia underwent continuous portable PSG recording. EEG analyses focused on six scalp channels (F3, F4, C3, C4, O1, and O2) across four clinically defined stages: baseline, induction, maintenance, and recovery. Relative spectral power, spectral edge frequency at 95% cumulative power (SEF95), and spindle-like event metrics were quantified. Sensor-level functional connectivity was assessed using weighted phase-lag index, imaginary coherence, and amplitude envelope correlation (AEC). Spectral and spindle-like event measures were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, and connectivity differences were assessed using permutation-based paired tests with false discovery rate correction. Relative delta power decreased from baseline and induction to maintenance and recovery, whereas theta, alpha, sigma, and beta relative power and SEF95 generally increased. Spindle-like event density differed across stages and was highest during recovery, while mean duration and peak frequency remained relatively stable within the 11-16 Hz range. Functional connectivity showed metric-specific modulation: AEC demonstrated the most widespread stage-related differences, whereas phase-based connectivity measures showed only limited edge-specific changes after correction for multiple comparisons. Portable PSG-derived six-channel EEG captured stage-related spectral, spindle-like event, and sensor-level connectivity changes during propofol anesthesia for GI endoscopy. These findings identify candidate EEG features for future evaluation of emergence detection and atypical anesthetic-state identification during procedural anesthesia. Their utility for real-time propofol titration or excessive-sedation warning requires prospective validation.

These findings identify candidate EEG markers for anesthetic state transitions.

papers.title: Sleep stage-specific heart rate variability feature-driven clustering analysis: identifying cardiac autonomic endotypes with long-term cardiovascular predictive value.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular risk assessment in obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) has traditionally relied on the Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI). However, AHI primarily reflects respiratory event burden and may not adequately capture inter-individual heterogeneity in sleep-related cardiorespiratory regulation. This study aimed to identify sleep stage-specific heart rate variability (HRV) phenotypes and evaluate their associations with long-term cardiovascular outcomes. Data were obtained from the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS). After exclusion of participants with missing clinical covariates or outcome data, 4029 individuals were included. Linear and non-linear HRV features were extracted from stage-specific electrocardiographic segments during N2, N3, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. K-means clustering was performed independently for each sleep stage after Z-score standardization, and the optimal cluster number was determined using silhouette coefficients and the elbow method. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to evaluate associations between HRV-informed phenotypes and all-cause mortality, coronary heart disease, and cardiovascular disease (CVD). Three HRV-informed phenotypes were identified within the selected clustering framework across N2, N3, and REM sleep stages: Stable (Cluster 0), Burden (Cluster 1), and High risk (Cluster 2). Compared with the Stable phenotype, the High-risk phenotype was consistently associated with increased cardiovascular risk, with the strongest association observed for incident CVD in the N2 stage [hazard ratio (HR) 1.468, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.280-1.684, P < 0.001]. Similar associations were observed in the N3 (HR 1.426, 95% CI 1.249-1.629, P < 0.001) and REM (HR 1.394, 95% CI 1.216-1.598, P < 0.001) stages. Sequential adjustment for AHI, oxygen desaturation index, arousal index, and sleep efficiency resulted in only minimal attenuation of hazard estimates, indicating that the prognostic associations were largely independent of conventional respiratory severity measures. In contrast, the Burden phenotype was consistently associated with lower all-cause mortality across all three sleep stages (HR 0.83-0.85, all P < 0.001). Subgroup analyses stratified by OSA severity demonstrated broadly consistent prognostic associations across AHI strata. Incorporating sleep stage-specific HRV features into conventional clinical phenotyping provides complementary prognostic information beyond traditional respiratory severity metrics. HRV-informed phenotyping may improve long-term cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with OSA.

papers.title: The spatial extent of fast ripples is associated with cognitive and language deficits in children with focal epilepsy: An exploratory SEEG study.
papers.abstract: To determine if the spatial extent of interictal fast ripples in focal epilepsy patients is associated with brain dysfunction. Thirty pediatric focal epilepsy patients who underwent SEEG investigation had their cognitive and language deficits assessed in scales of 0 to 4. Fast ripples (250-500 Hz), ripples (80-250 Hz), and IEDs were automatically detected in 10 min during NREM sleep. We fitted linear models to the relationship between the cognitive deficit scale and the spatial spread of the interictal neurophysiologic events (number of channels with rate of events > 10 % of maximum rate). For the language deficit, we computed the Spearman correlation between the median rate of events in all brain regions and the deficit scale. Cognitive deficit scale was significantly associated with the number of channels with fast ripples (p = 0.049), not so with ripples (p = 0.31), IEDs (p = 0.31). The potential confound of number of explored channels did not improve the fitting of the models. Language deficits were not correlated with the number of channels showing interictal events. However, from all brain regions the most statistically significant correlations (p < 0.01) were between median fast ripple rates in the left and right pars opercularis and triangularis of the inferior frontal gyrus (Broca's area and its contralateral counterpart) with r = 0.66, p = 0.003 (18 patients), in the superior temporal gyrus in the language dominant hemisphere with r = 0.72, p = 0.005 (13 patients), and the dominant basal temporal region with r = 0.79, p = 0.006 (10 patients). Median rates of IEDs and ripples exhibited lower correlation with language deficits in these regions. Widespread fast ripples are associated with increased cognitive deficits, and language deficiencies are correlated with fast ripple rates in brain regions associated with language. The extent of fast-ripple activity was associated with cognitive deficit severity in this cohort, whereas the corresponding associations for ripples and IEDs did not reach statistical significance.

papers.title: Sleep Duration and Mental Well-Being Among Older Chinese Adults: A Four-Wave Fixed-Effects Analysis Using CHARLS.
papers.abstract: To examine within-person associations between nighttime sleep duration and mental well-being among older Chinese adults. We analyzed four waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS; 2011-2018) using individual fixed-effects linear regressions with wave fixed effects and individual-clustered standard errors. Outcomes were CES-D-10 depressive symptoms and reverse-coded life satisfaction. Sleep was modeled continuously and categorically, with main categories of ≤6 h, >6 to <9 h, and ≥9 h; sensitivity models used ≤ 5 h, >5 to <9 h, and ≥9 h. Among observations with valid CES-D-10 data, 36.74% met the ≥10 screening threshold. Each additional hour of sleep was associated with lower CES-D-10 scores (β = -0.305) and higher life satisfaction (β = 0.015). Compared with the main reference range, short sleep was associated with higher CES-D-10 scores (β = 0.846) and lower life satisfaction (β = -0.046). Long-sleep estimates varied by specification and outcome. Shorter nighttime sleep duration, particularly sleep in the operational short-sleep category, was associated with poorer mental well-being within individuals over time. Usual sleep duration can inform mood and sleep assessment but should not substitute for evaluation of sleep quality or sleep disorders.

papers.title: Clinical and genetic correlates of a circadian subtype of depression in the Australian Genetics of Depression Study.
papers.abstract: Although commonly accepted depressive subtypes reflect phenotypic differences, there has been minimal progress in identification of discrete pathophysiological pathways, biomarkers or differential therapeutic approaches to effectively guide clinical management. To test the biological validity and clinical utility of a circadian subtype of depression on the basis of clinical course, differential medication response (self-reported) and genetic risk profile. Cross-sectional data were drawn from the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Participants were classified as having a 'circadian' or 'non-circadian' subtype of depression on the basis of meeting criteria for at least three binary circadian-associated features: social jetlag, seasonality, delayed sleep midpoint, evening chronotype, morning tiredness and hypersomnia. Clinical course characteristics were compared. Associations with response to commonly prescribed antidepressants and polygenic risk scores for mental disorders and sleep, circadian, metabolic and inflammatory traits were investigated using logistic regression models. A total of 2604 participants (23%; 80% female; mean age 37.87 ± 13.62 years) had a circadian subtype. They reported an earlier age at onset (P < 0.001), more severe clinical features including (hypo)manic-like and psychotic-like experiences, suicidality, psychological distress and somatic complaints (all P < 0.001), weight gain during depressive episodes (P < 0.001), poorer response to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.88 [95% CI 0.82, 0.94]) and serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.89 [95% CI 0.83, 0.97]), and more side-effects compared with those with a non-circadian subtype. Having a circadian subtype was associated with higher polygenic risk scores for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.17]), major depression (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), anxiety (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.04, 1.15]), bipolar disorder (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.04, 1.14]), body mass index (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.05, 1.14]), triglycerides (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), interleukin-6 (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]), higher insulin resistance (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.04, 1.13]), later sleep midpoint (odds ratio 1.15 [95% CI 1.10, 1.21]), insomnia (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]) and later chronotype (odds ratio 0.68 [95% CI 0.65, 0.71]). These findings support the face validity and potential clinical utility of a circadian subtype of depression as a clinical profile. Pending independent replication, investigation of its biology and predictive utility are warranted.

papers.title: Sleep, inflammation, and pain in musculoskeletal rehabilitation: a structured integrative review of neurobiological mechanisms and non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance, inflammation, and persistent pain may reinforce one another, compromising musculoskeletal rehabilitation. To synthesize evidence on mechanisms linking sleep, inflammation, and pain and identify relevant non-pharmacological interventions. This structured integrative review examined peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to December 2025, identified through PubMed, Scopus, PEDro, and SciELO. Reporting and synthesis were guided by SANRA and EQUATOR recommendations. Fifty-seven studies were included: 24 experimental or observational studies, 17 systematic reviews or meta-analyses, and 16 narrative or integrative reviews. Sleep restriction was associated with changes in interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein, with responses varying across populations and protocols. Prostaglandins and bradykinin may promote nociceptive sensitization, while disrupted sleep may impair descending pain inhibition. Exercise, manual therapy, neuromuscular electrical stimulation, low-level laser therapy, and sleep-focused behavioral interventions showed mechanistic plausibility, although confirmatory trials remain limited. Sleep assessment and sleep-focused interventions should be considered within multimodal musculoskeletal pain management, while further controlled research clarifies clinical effectiveness.

papers.title: Beyond the pump: a narrative review of the acute molecular, metabolic, and neuropsychological responses to a bout of resistance exercise.
papers.abstract: Resistance training is widely recognized for its chronic adaptations, including strength, muscle hypertrophy, and improvements in musculoskeletal health. However, a single bout of resistance exercise also elicits a range of acute physiological and psychological responses across multiple systems. These immediate responses have generally been examined within individual physiological domains, with less attention given to their coexistence and temporal overlap following a single session. This narrative review synthesizes evidence relating to the acute systemic effects of a single bout of resistance exercise. Literature was identified through iterative searches of electronic databases and reference lists, with emphasis on primary human studies directly examining acute responses, alongside relevant systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and mechanistic literature. Acute resistance exercise induces responses across endocrine and myokine, metabolic, vascular, pain-related, psychological, cognitive, and sleep-related domains. Contracting skeletal muscle releases myokines and other signalling molecules with potential systemic actions. Post-exercise energy expenditure and muscle protein synthesis may remain elevated during recovery, while glucose uptake and insulin sensitivity are enhanced. Acute resistance exercise can also produce exercise-induced hypoalgesia, reduce state anxiety, improve aspects of executive function and cognitive performance, and may influence sleep continuity and neurophysiological activity. These responses differ in their evidential basis and physiological significance, encompassing directly observed short-term effects, proposed regulatory mechanisms, and more tentative hypotheses regarding longer-term implications. A single bout of resistance exercise produces temporally overlapping responses across multiple physiological and psychological systems. These responses should not be assumed to represent adaptive remodelling or direct mechanisms of chronic health benefit. Nevertheless, integrating them provides a broader perspective on the immediate multisystem consequences of resistance exercise and may help inform future research examining how repeated acute responses relate to longer-term adaptation and health outcomes.

papers.title: Preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal cord D2R expression via the PP2A/AKT-dependent NMDA receptor phosphorylation.
papers.abstract: Preoperative sleep deprivation (SD) is known to exacerbate postoperative pain, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using a male mouse model of 48-hour continuous SD followed by incisional surgery, we found that SD alone induced transient mechanical hyperalgesia, and when combined with surgery (SI group) it significantly aggravated and prolonged postoperative pain recovery until day 10. On postoperative day 7, SI mice showed marked downregulation of spinal dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) expression and decreased spinal dopamine concentration. D2R was predominantly expressed on spinal glutamatergic neurons. Overexpression of D2R on these neurons via intrathecal AAV injection effectively alleviated the prolonged hyperalgesia, normalizing pain sensitivity by day 7. Mechanistically, D2R downregulation led to increased phosphorylation of NMDA receptor subunits (p-NR1 and p-NR2B) without altering total NMDA receptor levels. Co-immunoprecipitation revealed an interaction between D2R and protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A). SI mice exhibited decreased PP2A expression but increased p-AKT, p-GSK3β, and β-catenin, indicating activation of the PP2A/AKT signaling pathway, which were reversed by D2R overexpression. Furthermore, pharmacological activation of PP2A with DT-061 not only downregulated p-AKT, p-GSK3β, β-catenin, p-NR1 and p-NR2B, but also produced significant analgesia in SI mice. Collectively, these results demonstrate that preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal D2R on glutamatergic neurons, which disinhibits the PP2A/AKT pathway and enhances NMDA receptor phosphorylation. Targeting D2R or its downstream PP2A/AKT signaling may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for managing persistent postoperative pain caused by preoperative sleep deprivation in male mice.

papers.title: Heart rate rises most during REM sleep after semaglutide initiation: a matched longitudinal cohort study
papers.abstract: Study Objectives: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists raise resting heart rate. We asked whether, after semaglutide initiation, the increase is larger during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep than during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep. Methods: In the Human Phenotype Project, an Israeli cohort of generally healthy adults aged 40 to 70 years, 96 of 494 self-reported semaglutide initiators had a home sleep study (WatchPAT; sleep stages estimated from peripheral arterial tone and actigraphy) before and at least three months after starting. Each was propensity-matched 1:1 to a never-user of GLP-1 drugs measured at the same visits. We estimated the initiators' change minus their controls' change (difference-in-differences). The REM minus NREM contrast was designated primary after an exploratory analysis. Results: Relative to controls (90 to 94 pairs), heart rate rose during nocturnal wake (+3.89 beats per minute [bpm], 95% confidence interval 2.35 to 5.44), NREM sleep (+4.82 bpm, 3.12 to 6.52) and REM sleep (+6.25 bpm, 4.42 to 7.91); the REM increase exceeded the NREM increase by 1.42 bpm (0.98 to 1.89). The excess persisted across matching designs and on a relative scale; the proportion of REM sleep did not change. Never-users with similar weight loss showed no REM sleep heart-rate rise (+0.40 bpm, -0.63 to 1.50). Heart-rate variability decreases disappeared after adjustment for heart rate. Conclusions: Semaglutide initiation was associated with higher heart rate throughout sleep, most during REM sleep, unexplained by weight loss. Clinic measurements may understate this effect. Confirmation with polysomnographic staging is needed.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Sequencing Identifies Altered Expression of Circadian Rhythm-Related Genes Pomc and Bmp4 in Post-Stroke Depression.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a serious complication that significantly hinders stroke patients' recovery and quality of life. Uncovering the molecular changes that drive PSD is vital for understanding how depression develops following a stroke. In this study, we established a reproducible PSD model using minimally invasive photochemical-induced focal cortical lesion. Transcriptomic sequencing demonstrated that dysregulation of circadian entrainment genes is a central pathway in the development of post-stroke depressive-like behaviors. Protein-protein interaction network analysis of these circadian rhythm-related genes identified six hub genes. Four of these, including Pomc and Bmp4, exhibited expression patterns consistent with experimental validation. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic analysis further pinpointed cell-type-specific expression abnormalities of Pomc in endothelial cells and Bmp4 in oligodendrocytes. Subsequently, in silico perturbation analysis further indicated that their shared underlying regulatory mechanisms involve cell adhesion and extracellular matrix interaction. Collectively, using transcriptomic and single-cell sequencing in a PSD model, this study revealed altered expression patterns of circadian rhythm-related genes, providing potential targets for further investigation into the pathogenesis of PSD.

papers.title: An examination of the effect of dual task on gait in Parkinson's disease and REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.abstract: Gait variability is a hallmark of Parkinson's disease (PD) and has been linked to cognitive deficits and fall risk. Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) is a strong predictor of synucleinopathies, yet evidence for gait changes in RBD is inconsistent. Performing a dual task increases gait variability, an effect that can be quantified using a cost function. Determine the degree to which dual task cost differs between control, RBD, and PD participants at baseline, and between RBD converters versus non-converters at follow-up. 46 RBD, 23 control, and 14 PD participants completed standardized gait analysis at baseline. Parameters chosen a priori for analysis included enhanced gait variability index (eGVI), functional ambulation performance (FAP), velocity, step length, cadence, base of support, and double support time. Medical records were surveilled for 3 years following participant enrollment, determining that 6 RBD participants converted to Parkinsonism. Baseline gait indices and dual task costs were compared between control, RBD, and PD groups at enrollment, and between RBD stable and RBD converters at follow-up. The PD group had greater eGVI, as well as greater dual task cost for FAP, cadence, width, and double support time. No differences in gait variability or cost were identified between RBD and control groups at baseline. Compared to the stable group, RBD converters had greater dual task cost for FAP, velocity, cadence, and double support time. Increases in dual task cost for specific gait parameters may identify RBD patients at imminent risk of phenoconversion.

papers.title: [Neurocognitive characteristics in children with sluggish cognitive tempo].
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to assess the neurocognitive characteristics of children diagnosed with sluggish cognitive tempo (SCT) and to evaluate the efficacy of Cortexin in addressing this condition. The main study group included 40 children aged 12 to 14 years with symptoms consistent with SCT manifestations. The comparison group consisted of 30 children with combined ADHD (ADHD-C), also aged 12 to 14 years. The control group comprised 30 children in the same age range without any neuropsychiatric disorders. The study used several methods, including S. Lee's SCT scale for assessing the severity of SCT symptoms, the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI-20), the Daytime Sleepiness Scale, and T.A. Fotekova and T.V. Akhutina's reading skills assessment method, the «Working Memory» method to quantifying working memory capabilities, the TOVA computer test, and EEG (routine and spectral analysis). Cortexin was administered intramuscularly at a standard dosage of 10 mg every other day across 10 injections to patients diagnosed with SCT. The study results showed that children with SCT, in comparison to their counterparts with ADHD-C and healthy peers, exhibited significantly more pronounced asthenic symptoms and a higher prevalence of comorbid learning disorders. Quantitative EEG analysis revealed a reduced theta-to-alpha wave power ratio in the anterior cerebral cortex of the SCT group compared with the ADHD cohort. These findings support the hypothesis that children with SCT are less prone to exhibiting deficits in inhibition processes, while instead demonstrating a decline in overall levels of functional activity maintenance. A follow-up assessment after treatment revealed improvements in inattention, severity of working memory impairment, asthenic symptoms, and reading skills in 82% of cases. Additionally, EEG analysis post-treatment indicated a reduction in alpha-band power in the frontal and central leads of both hemispheres, suggesting enhanced overall cortical activation. This study has delineated several cognitive characteristics associated with SCT in children and demonstrated that administering Cortexin significantly alleviates the primary symptoms of SCT and mitigates the manifestation of major comorbid disorders.

papers.title: Modification of locomotion-respiration coupling in patients with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome.
papers.abstract: Locomotion is a complex motor task integrating sensory-motor and cognitive inputs through central pattern generator control. Locomotion-respiration coupling (LRC), defined as the synchronization between gait and breathing events, has been described during running and walking. Patients with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) exhibit altered gait patterns during wakefulness, which appear to be partially independent of nocturnal symptomatic treatment. While intermittent hypoxia may induce long-term ("fixed") central nervous system alterations, OSAS patients also display "reversible" adaptive mechanisms during wakefulness aimed at preventing upper airway (UA) collapse, involving changes in respiratory control and posture. Whether these adaptive mechanisms affect LRC and contribute to gait alterations remains unknown. Ten awake patients with controlled OSAS treated with a mandibular advancement device (MAD) and ten matched healthy controls performed a one-minute walking trial on an instrumented treadmill with motion capture. Ventilation was assessed via thoracic expansion, and spatiotemporal gait parameters were extracted from kinematic and force platform data. LRC was quantified using phase-locking values (PLV) between ventilatory events and sagittal-plane joint kinematics. OSAS patients were assessed both with and without their MAD. Compared with controls, OSAS patients exhibited a longer double-stance phase and a shorter swing phase. Expiratory events occurred preferentially during double stance in OSAS patients, whereas controls showed a higher occurrence during swing. PLV analysis revealed increased synchronization between inspiratory events and hip and knee motion, as well as between expiratory events and trunk and hip motion in OSAS patients. These significative differences were no longer observed when patients wore their MAD. Logistic regression demonstrated that PLV metrics of inspiratory-hip and expiratory-trunk coupling effectively discriminated OSAS patients from controls, but not when UA stabilization was applied. Awake patients with controlled OSAS exhibit altered gait patterns characterized by increased locomotion-respiration coupling. This heightened synchronization likely reflects adaptive, reversible strategies aimed at limiting UA collapsibility during wakefulness rather than fixed hypoxia-related impairments alone. LRC may represent a functional marker of daytime motor alterations in OSAS and a potential target for interventions addressing UA mechanics beyond nocturnal treatment.

papers.title: Integrating task-state electroencephalography and motor function for intelligent assessment of recovery status from prolonged disorders of consciousness.
papers.abstract: Accurately assessing recovery in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness (PDoC) is essential for evaluating the therapeutic efficacy and optimizing clinical care. However, substantial individual variability and poorly understood recovery mechanisms render this task exceptionally challenging. We collected task-state electroencephalography and clinical records from 78 PDoC patients to develop an intelligent assessment framework. Power spectral densities (PSDs) and coherence values (CVs) derived from event-related potentials (ERPs) were extracted and integrated with motor function scores to construct a multidimensional feature set. Linear support vector machine (SVM) and logistic regression (LR) models were built and rigorously evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was utilized for visual explanation. The LOOCV indicated that both LR and SVM achieved optimal, similar performance in integrating alpha-band features with motor function (Macro-Average F1-score [Ma-F]: 76.79% versus 75.54%). The Receiver Operating Characteristic curves (with Area Under the Curve values of 77.57% for LR and 72.82% for SVM) and Precision-Recall curves (with Average Precision values of 68.87% for LR and 59.85% for SVM) suggested that the framework performs stably. The reliability curves indicated that both models demonstrate good calibration and are reliable for assessment. The study provides preliminary evidence that alpha-band PSDs and CVs derived from ERPs potentially enhance the motor function assessment performance. This integrated paradigm provides a valuable indicator. Overall, our findings suggest that combining neuroscience with intelligent technology holds promise for improving personalized diagnosis and optimizing the PDoC management.

papers.title: [Spectral-topographic features of EEG in patients with varying rates of alcohol dependence progression].
papers.abstract: To compare the spectral-topographic characteristics of the background electroencephalogram (EEG) in patients with alcohol dependence, differing in disease progression rate, as part of a pilot study. A total of 40 male patients with a confirmed diagnosis of alcohol dependence (F10.2 according to ICD-10) were examined. Utilizing a retrospective evaluation of the development of alcohol withdrawal syndrome (AWS), participants were classified into two distinct groups: those exhibiting rapid progression (≤3 years, n=23) and those with slow progression (≥12 years, n=17). Background EEG recordings were obtained using a 16-channel system (10-20 configuration), followed by spectral analysis of absolute power in the theta, alpha-1, alpha-2, beta-1, and beta-2 frequency bands. The analysis revealed that patients with rapid progression demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in the spectral power of the alpha-1 rhythm across all cortical regions (p<0.002 after correction), with the most pronounced effects observed in frontal and central leads. There were also reductions noted in the power of alpha-2, theta (except the parietal region), and beta-1 (limited to the frontal area) frequency bands. Notably, 74% of patients with rapid progression exhibited a low-amplitude («flattened») EEG pattern, whereas 71% in the slow progression group maintained a normal alpha rhythm. The results indicate the presence of a distinct neurophysiological endophenotype associated with the rapid progression of alcohol dependence. Key characteristics of this endophenotype include a overall decrease in the power of the alpha-1 rhythm, particularly in the front-central leads; a decline in theta power (excluding the parietal region); a frontal-specific reduction in beta-1 power; and a significant prevalence of low-amplitude EEG patterns.

papers.title: Effects of EEG neurofeedback in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review of randomised and non-randomised studies.
papers.abstract: Pharmacotherapy is recommended as the first-line treatment for adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), yet some individuals show partial or inadequate response associated with adverse effects. These limitations have prompted interest in adjunctive or alternative interventions. Electroencephalography (EEG) neurofeedback is a non-pharmacological intervention for ADHD, which enables self-regulation of neural activity. This systematic review synthesised clinical, cognitive, and electrophysiological outcomes of EEG neurofeedback in adult ADHD, and examined standard versus personalised training protocols. Following PRISMA guidelines, four databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, Ovid, Web of Science) were searched from 1960 to October 2025 for this PROSPERO-registered review (ID: CRD420251020898). Eligible studies included adults (≥ 18 years) with a formal ADHD diagnosis undergoing EEG neurofeedback. Outcomes comprised symptom severity, cognitive performance, electrophysiology, and adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I V2. Seven studies (three RCTs, four non-randomised; n = 390) met inclusion criteria. Protocols included theta/beta (n = 1), slow cortical potential (n = 1), alpha downregulation training (n = 1) and personalised approaches guided by individual alpha peak frequency (n = 3) or QEEG profiles (n = 1). Naturalistic and personalised studies reported large symptom reductions, whereas RCTs revealed small, generally non-significant effects relative to controls. Cognitive improvements were inconsistently reported and largely attributable to practice effects. Electrophysiological changes were protocol-specific without convergence across studies. No treatment-related adverse events were observed. Evidence remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, small samples, variable controls, inconsistent learning metrics, and risk of bias. Current RCTs do not demonstrate evidence of efficacy over placebo. Blinded, adequately powered trials using standardised learning measures are needed to clarify mechanisms of neurofeedback.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea is frequent in patients with Long COVID fatigue but is not significantly associated with alterations of quality of life and cognition.
papers.abstract: Neurologic manifestations of Long COVID, also called post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), include fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, sleep disturbances, and headaches, which can be debilitating. Since these symptoms overlap with those of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), we sought to determine the prevalence of OSA in the population of a Neuro-COVID-19 clinic. We performed home sleep testing in 100 consecutive patients with Long COVID and no prior history of OSA who reported fatigue after an episode of COVID-19 not requiring hospitalization. The average age was 46.4 years and 70% of patients were female. OSA was present in 53% of patients, including 33% with mild OSA (apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 5-14.9) and 20% with moderate to severe OSA (AHI ≥ 15). Male sex, higher age, and body mass index were significantly associated with OSA. However, there were no significant differences in other comorbidities, Long COVID symptom burden, quality of life measures (QoL), and objective cognitive function test results between groups. Additionally, multiple linear regression models demonstrated that neither AHI nor mean desaturation nadir were significant predictors of QoL or cognitive function. Although OSA is nearly twice as prevalent among our study participants compared to the general adult population of the US, it was not significantly associated with Long COVID symptoms, alteration of QoL, or objective cognitive dysfunction. However, 20% of patients were diagnosed with moderate to severe OSA, a clinically significant finding that warrants intervention to prevent irreversible cardiopulmonary complications.

papers.title: EEG microstate alterations in psychotic depression: prolonged microstate C duration and associations with psychotic symptoms.
papers.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (MDD-Psy) represents a severe clinical subtype with distinct psychopathology, yet its underlying large-scale brain network dynamics, as measured by resting-state EEG microstates, remain poorly characterized. We compared 68 patients with MDD-Psy and 63 patients with MDD without psychotic features (MDD-NonPsy). Clinical assessment included the Kangduo Antidepressant Scale (KDAS) and the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS). Resting-state EEG microstate parameters (duration, time coverage, occurrence, and transition probabilities) were analyzed. Group comparisons employed Mann-Whitney U/t-tests with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction. Correlations between microstate alterations and psychotic symptom severity were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation with FDR correction. The groups were comparable in age and sex. The MDD-Psy group exhibited significantly greater severity in thought disturbance, activation, and hostility (all p < 0.001). EEG microstate analysis revealed a significantly prolonged median duration of microstate C, putatively associated with salience-network-related activity in MDD-Psy (91.99 ms) versus MDD-NonPsy (85.56 ms; p-corr = 0.004). Altered transition probabilities characterized MDD-Psy, including increased B→A but decreased B→C and C→A transitions (all p-corr < 0.05). Furthermore, in the combined sample, the duration of microstate C positively correlated with thought disturbance (ρ = 0.243, p-FDR = 0.030), while the reduced B→C transition probability was strongly negatively correlated with both thought disturbance (ρ=-0.393, p-FDR < 0.001) and hostility. Within patients with major depressive disorder, the psychotic subtype is associated with a distinct pattern of aberrant resting-state brain network dynamics relative to the non-psychotic subtype, characterized by prolonged microstate C duration, commonly linked to salience network dynamics and reconfigured temporal transitions between the salience, visual, and auditory networks. The altered visual-to-salience network transition (B → C) demonstrated the most robust association with core psychotic symptom dimensions, including thought disturbance and hostility. These findings suggest that dysregulated dynamic coupling between perceptual processing and salience evaluation may represent a candidate neurophysiological indicator of psychotic features in depression. However, these results should be considered hypothesis-generating preliminary: the high rate of antipsychotic medication use in the MDD-Psy group, the absence of a healthy control group, and the cross-sectional design preclude tentative causal or specificity claims. Future longitudinal studies incorporating medication-naïve patients, healthy controls, and complementary neurophysiological markers are required to validate the clinical utility of these microstate alterations. papers.title: Quantitative Analysis of Electroencephalography in Hypnosis: A Neurophysiological Approach.
papers.abstract: Hypnosis is a unique state of consciousness marked by heightened response to suggestions, focused attention, and altered cognitive control. This article explores the neural connections involved in hypnosis through electroencephalography (EEG) studies, examining brain changes during hypnosis and their relationship to hypnotic depth and susceptibility. Theta waves, linked to hypnotic depth, are stronger in highly hypnotizable individuals, while gamma waves are associated with focus, suggestion acceptance, and emotional responses. Hypnosis also induces frequency-dependent reorganization of large-scale brain connectivity, particularly in frontal-parietal and attentional networks, enhancing subjective experiences and responsiveness. EEG patterns reveal more dynamic neural activity during hypnosis, which cannot be captured by linear metrics alone. Hemispheric analysis shows greater left-hemisphere activity in highly hypnotizable individuals, particularly in emotionally and verbally mediated tasks, challenging the right-hemisphere dominance model. Event related potential (ERP) findings show that hypnosis affects information processing at both pre-attentional and cognitive levels. These insights contribute to understanding hypnosis' impact on the brain and its potential for personalized therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: Progress in research on the bidirectional relationship between circadian rhythm and depression: A bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: This study used VOSviewer and CiteSpace to conduct a bibliometric analysis of 444 publications on the relationship between circadian rhythms and depression, retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (January 2015 to April 2025). Publication numbers remained low until 2017 but increased markedly after 2018, with the United States contributing the largest share. Ian B. Hickie and Joanne S. Carpenter were the most prolific authors; the University of Pittsburgh and Chronobiology International were the most productive institution and journal, respectively. McClung, Dubocovich, and Logan were the top co-cited authors, while frequent keywords included "expression," "sleep," "circadian rhythms," and "melatonin." These findings underscore the growing importance of circadian rhythms in depression pathophysiology and therapy, with future research likely to focus on diagnosis, biomarker identification, individualized treatment, prognosis, and health management.

papers.title: Persistent postoperative pediatric pain: a secondary analysis of the 4P prospective observational multicenter study.
papers.abstract: Few large studies have examined the prevalence and risk factors for persistent postoperative pain (PPOP) in children. Chronic pain in childhood can lead to significant personal suffering, including non-attendance at school and social isolation. In a prospective observational multicenter study, we followed 601 children undergoing common pediatric surgeries. This secondary analysis aimed to describe the prevalence, characteristics, and exploratory risk factor associations of PPOP. The primary outcome was defined as recurrent pain (4 on an age-specific scale lasting for over three months after surgery. Persistent pain was further characterized regarding its impact on various activities and whether it was anatomically localized at the site of surgery. Of the 601 children, 380 were available for follow-up at 3 and 6 months after surgery. The median age was 5 years, and 34% were female. Preoperative pain was reported by 41 children (11%), and 126 (33%) reported anxiety or sleep problems before surgery. Thirteen (3%) patients experienced PPOP (≥ 4) after either 3 (n = 9) or 6 months (n = 4). Ten attributed the pain to the surgical area, and in six children, the pain affected activity-levels. Five children used analgesics for their symptoms. Only one child experienced pain daily, and three children reported weekly pain. Applying a stricter definition from ICD-11 to our cohort resulted in an even lower PPOP prevalence: only three (0.8%) children experienced pain lasting more than 3 months, in whom the pain began or increased after surgery, was at a level ≥4, influenced activity-levels, and was located in the surgical area. The prevalence of persistent postoperative pain after common pediatric surgeries was very low. As one of the few prospective multicenter studies in this field, these findings are noteworthy.

papers.title: Longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and their association with cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity risk in postmenopausal women: evidence from the CHARLS study.
papers.abstract: To investigate the association between longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and the risk of cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity (CRMM) in a population of postmenopausal women. A total of 2,859 postmenopausal women from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) were included, with 4 repeated measurements of night sleep duration collected from 2011 to 2018. Group-based trajectory modeling was adopted to identify distinct sleep duration trajectory patterns. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations between sleep trajectories and incident CRMM ascertained between 2018 and 2020. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses were further conducted to validate the robustness of the findings. Three sleep duration trajectory patterns were identified: normal-stable (33.9% of the cohort), normal-fluctuating decline (52.0%), and short-rapid decline (14.1%). During a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome (incident CRMM) occurred in 108 participants (3.8%). Compared with normal-stable group, those in normal-fluctuating decline and short-rapid decline groups had an increased risk of CRMM (ORs of 2.30 [95%CI, 1.35-3.91] and 3.75 [95%CI, 1.99-7.07], respectively) after adjustment for multiple covariates. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these associations, which were independent of key baseline characteristics and missing data. In postmenopausal women, short and declining sleep duration trajectories are strong, independent risk factors for CRMM. Public health and clinical interventions should prioritize maintaining stable, adequate sleep to mitigate multimorbidity risk in this population.

papers.title: Comparative effects of exercise modalities on sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders: A systematic review with pairwise, network, and dose-responsemeta-analyses.
papers.abstract: Exercise may improve sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders, but the comparative effects of different exercise modalities and the dose-response relationship remain unclear. We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to May 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials examining the effects of exercise interventions on sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders. Two independent reviewers assessed study quality, and random-effects pairwise, network, and dose-response meta-analyses were performed to evaluate the effects of different exercise interventions and doses on sleep quality. The analysis included 23 randomized controlled trials involving 1,478 middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders. Pairwise meta-analysis showed that exercise reduced Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) scores but had no significant effect on Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) scores. Bayesian network meta-analysis showed that, compared with the control group, aerobic exercise (SMD = 1.34, 95% CrI: 0.86∼1.82), mind-body exercise (SMD = 0.64, 95% CrI: 0.30∼0.97), and combined exercise (SMD = 0.60, 95% CrI: 0.13∼1.07) may improve PSQI scores. The dose-response analysis suggested an inverted U-shaped association, with the largest predicted effect occurring near 539 MET-min/week within the observed dose range. Low-to moderate-certainty evidence suggests that aerobic, mind-body, and combined exercise may reduce PSQI scores, with a nonlinear dose-response relationship.

papers.title: Combined eye tracking and electroencephalography during referential selection in dyadic interaction.
papers.abstract: Understanding language in real-world interaction requires methods that integrate auditory, visual, and neural signals. We present a proof-of-concept study combining mobile electroencephalography (EEG) and eye tracking to investigate referential selection during dyadic communication. Using a simplified version of the director task, pairs of participants engaged in naturalistic object-movement instructions while EEG and gaze data were recorded and synchronized via LabStreamingLayer, allowing us to calculate overlap-corrected, regression-based event-related potentials (rERPs) time-locked to spoken nouns and to participants' fixations, focusing on the N400/P300 (300-500 ms) and later (500-800 ms) time windows. Our results show that gaze behavior and fixation-related potentials provide crucial information for interpreting language-related ERPs: Targets competing with occluded referents elicited a stronger posterior positivity consistent with greater attentional demands. Fixation timing systematically modulated neural responses. Contrary to predictions, competitors received little visual attention, indicating that participants prioritized task-relevant information. These findings highlight the potential of multimodal data integration for understanding attentional and predictive mechanisms in real-world communication. Importantly, we show that established analytic techniques, such as artifact subspace reconstruction, independent component analysis, and linear deconvolution for ERP calculation, apply to noisy, naturalistic datasets. In addition, we provide a subsampling sensitivity approach to test the stability of the effects across different sample sizes. This study provides a methodological framework linking gaze and neural activity during interactive language processing. All preprocessing and analysis scripts, along with example datasets, are openly available on OSF ( https://osf.io/5ds4z ; a modified and optimized Python implementation is also available on GitHub: https://github.com/XlinCLab/DGAME ).

papers.title: Apnea-hypopnea index-oxygen desaturation index (AHI-ODI) discordance in obstructive sleep apnea: association with symptom burden and cardiometabolic comorbidity: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) counts respiratory events but not the depth or duration of accompanying desaturation. We examined AHI-ODI discordance (AHI minus oxygen desaturation index, ODI) and its associations with daytime symptom burden and prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity. Single-center retrospective cross-sectional study of 200 adults with OSA (January 2023-January 2025). Five indices (AHI, ODI, mean SpO2, T90 and AHI-ODI discordance) were examined; excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS; Epworth Sleepiness Scale ≥ 11) was the primary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI and an AHI-ODI × sex interaction. The cohort was 77.5% male, median age 57 years (48.8-64.2). For EDS, AHI-ODI discordance showed the numerically highest AUC (0.639, p < 0.001), followed by T90 (0.627), and mean SpO2 and ODI (0.609 each); AHI was not significant (0.546, p = 0.264). No pairwise difference was significant. AHI-ODI discordance remained independently associated with EDS after adjustment (OR 1.04 per event/h, 95% CI 1.01-1.07, p = 0.008), with no significant sex interaction. Among secondary outcomes, T90 showed the highest AUCs for diabetes mellitus (0.644) and hypertension (0.615), and mean SpO2 for heart failure (0.608). No index discriminated against previous stroke or atrial fibrillation. AHI-ODI discordance was independently, but only modestly, associated with EDS, whereas oxygenation indices were related to prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity. The discrimination was insufficient, and all reported cut-offs are exploratory. AHI-ODI discordance is not a measure of sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden.

papers.title: [The correlation of interleukin 2 and interleukin 4 with alterations in the brachiocephalic arteries in patients with obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.abstract: To evaluate the relationship between interleukin 2 (IL-2) and interleukin 4 (IL-4) and the alterations occurring in the extracranial levels of arteries of patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). A total of 65 subjects participated in the study, comprising 40 males (61.5%) and 25 females (38.5%), with a mean age of 52.86±9.75 years. The subjects were categorized into two distinct groups: the main group, consisting of 37 patients with OSA and an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) of more than 15 episodes per hour, and the control group, consisting of 28 subjects without OSA and an AHI of less than 5 episodes per hour. The diagnostic procedure for all subjects encompassed anthropometric measurements, polysomnography, and ultrasound imaging of the brachiocephalic arteries (BCA). The assessment of chronic cerebral ischemia (CCI) and hypertension (HTN) was conducted. IL-2 and IL-4 levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Among patients diagnosed with OSA, CCI was detected in 75.7% of cases, and atherosclerotic changes in the BCA were observed in 89.2%. Furthermore, these patients presented with a bilateral increase in the diameters of the common carotid artery (CCA) and the internal carotid artery (ICA) (p<0.05), alongside a noted increase in IL-2 levels and a significantly reduced IL-4 levels. In the main group, a positive correlation was established between the diameter of the left ICA and IL-4 (r=0.421, p=0.009), as well as between the diameter of the right ICA and IL-4 (r=0.482, p=0.003). A positive association was also observed between the detected atherosclerotic alterations and neck circumference (r=0.269, p=0.030), AHI (r=0.255, p=0.041), HTN (r=0.336, p=0.006), and CCI (r=0.255, p=0.041). The findings of this study demonstrate that patients with OSA exhibit increasingly persistent and significant abnormalities in the extracranial arteries as the pathological process advances. The noted dilation of the ICA and the CCA in the main group is likely due to vascular remodeling and reduced IL-4 levels. The established correlation between atherosclerotic changes in the BCA and metrics such as neck circumference, AHI, HTN, and CCI suggests that OSA may directly induce pathological processes in vascular walls, thereby contributing to the emergence of comorbid conditions. The absence of a definitive link between BCA atherosclerosis and IL-4 levels in OSA patients may be attributable to the relatively small sample size, warranting further research.

papers.title: [Experience in the implementation of a comprehensive non-pharmacological therapeutic program at the Center for Cognitive and Psycho-Emotional Health].
papers.abstract: To analyze the outcomes of a complex non-pharmacological treatment regimen administered to patients at the daytime hospital (DH) of the Center for Cognitive and Psycho-Emotional Health (CCPH) and to evaluate the changes in the cognitive and psycho-emotional state of the patients. The study included 103 patients attending the CCPH DH, with a mean age of 46.98±14.32 years; 76.7% were female. Participants were categorized into three distinct groups: Group 1 with predominantly cognitive impairments (CIs), Group 2 with predominantly psycho-emotional disorders, and Group 3 with sleep disorders. Cognitive and psycho-emotional statuses were assessed using widely accepted tests and assessment scales. Each participant underwent a tailored five-day course of non-pharmacological therapy, which integrated cognitive training, biofeedback-based electroencephalography training, physical therapy, and neurostimulation techniques. Treatment outcomes were assessed after the intervention. Following the therapeutic intervention, 91.26% of participants demonstrated clinical improvement, with the greatest improvement observed in Group 2 (96.6%). No deterioration in clinical status was noted among any of the patients, thereby affirming the safety of the therapeutic interventions. Neuropsychological test results indicated a statistically significant improvement across all three groups (p<0.05), reflected in enhanced cognitive metrics and a reduction in anxiety and depressive symptoms among patients with pre-dementia CIs, anxiety disorders, and chronic insomnia. While a tendency towards improvement was noted in patients with severe ICs, the changes did not reach statistical significance, particularly in patients with isolated depressive disorders, potentially due to the limited sample size. Moreover, patients within Group 3 showed improvements in sleep during the therapy. The findings suggest that a five-day non-pharmacological intervention with an integrated approach represents an effective and safe method for the maintenance and enhancement of cognitive and psycho-emotional health.

papers.title: Mapping mental health complexity in esports: an exploratory psychosocial network approach.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise in popularity of esports has brought increased attention to the unique mental health challenges faced by esports players, yet research in this area remains in its infancy. Early research suggests a substantial mental health burden and has examined associations between esports-specific stressors, mental health, and sleep disturbances. However, much of this work has relied on traditional methodologies, providing limited insight into how affective, psychosocial, sleep-related, and esports-specific indicators are organised within this competitive performance environment. To address this gap, we developed a bespoke 17-item questionnaire tailored for Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) network analysis, an exploratory approach for mapping the conditional dependency structure of complex multivariate systems such as mental health. A total of 1025 esports players from over 60 countries completed the survey. Game-related thought preoccupation, a core feature of gaming disorder, emerged as the most robust structural sink node, downstream of several psychosocial indicators, raising the hypothesis that it represents a compound indicator of broader upstream psychosocial strain. Depressed mood occupied an upstream position within the network, an observation that held more robustly for the psychopathological subnetwork as a whole than for depressed mood as the single source. Mental fatigue occupied an intermediate, connecting position between affective variables and the sleep and fatigue indicators. Its high prevalence, together with a positioning upstream of the sleep indicators, suggests that it may warrant closer examination in future research on training load, recovery, and sleep in esports, though this ordering rested on edges with moderate directional support. Emotion control and a sense of autonomy appeared to connect upstream affective distress with downstream esports-specific indicators such as esports-related stress, though was the least stable of the structural features identified. Collectively, these findings provide an exploratory map of how mental health-relevant indicators were organised in this performance environment, and generate concrete, testable hypotheses for future longitudinal, experimental, and intervention research.

papers.title: Voluntary wheel running selectively preserves skeletal muscle during pancreatic cancer cachexia despite persistent systemic alterations
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is frequently associated with cancer cachexia, involving alterations across multiple physiological systems. Whether distinct exercise paradigms similarly influence these compartments remains unclear. We compared voluntary wheel running (VWR) and treadmill running (TR) using an integrative physiological approach in a murine model of pancreatic cancer cachexia. Methods Male C57BL/6J mice bearing UN-KC-6141 pancreatic tumor cells were allocated to inactive control (CaCTL), VWR or TR groups and compared with healthy controls. Tumor progression, body composition, skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, hepatic metabolism, systemic inflammation, energy expenditure and behavior were assessed. Analysis of covariance determined whether tissue-mass differences remained evident after adjustment for tumor burden. Results UN-KC-6141 tumors induced a systemic cachectic phenotype involving skeletal muscle and adipose tissue wasting, hepatic metabolic remodeling, systemic inflammation and behavioral alterations. VWR slowed tumor growth, reduced final tumor mass, improved the body-weight trajectory and preserved lean and skeletal muscle mass, whereas TR did not reproduce these adaptations. Greater gastrocnemius mass with VWR remained evident after adjustment for tumor mass, indicating that reduced tumor burden alone was insufficient to account for muscle preservation. In contrast, adipose tissue wasting, hepatic metabolic remodeling and systemic inflammation remained largely unaffected. TR was also associated with a less favorable body-weight trajectory and greater fat mass loss than in inactive tumor-bearing mice. Exploratory metabolic phenotyping revealed distinct feeding, sleep and resting energy expenditure patterns between the two exercise paradigms. Conclusions VWR selectively preserved skeletal muscle within a persistently altered systemic environment, whereas the TR protocol used here did not reproduce these adaptations. These findings reveal tissue-specific exercise responsiveness during pancreatic cancer cachexia and highlight exercise paradigm characteristics as determinants of tumor-host adaptation.

papers.title: An incidental heterozygous ATP7B nonsense variant leading to a diagnostic pitfall for Wilson disease: a pediatric case report.
papers.abstract: Wilson disease (WD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by pathogenic variants in ATP7B, resulting in impaired copper transport and progressive copper accumulation, most prominently affecting the liver. With the growing use of genetic testing, incidental detection of ATP7B pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in individuals without typical hepatic phenotypes can prompt overdiagnosis and unnecessary investigations. This case highlights the importance of interpreting a single heterozygous ATP7B variant in the context of phenotype and a standardized biochemical diagnostic pathway for WD. A 13-year-old Han Chinese boy presented with recurrent brief paroxysmal attacks for > 1 year, markedly worsened over the preceding month. Episodes were triggered by rising from sitting, characterized by transient postural instability with unilateral head deviation and ipsilateral dystonic/choreiform movements, lasted ~ 10 s, and resolved spontaneously. Consciousness was preserved, with no incontinence, convulsions, or postictal symptoms. Interictal neurological examination was normal. Ambulatory EEG monitoring captured three typical attacks without epileptiform discharges or ictal EEG correlates, and brain MRI was unremarkable. A slit-lamp examination revealed no Kayser-Fleischer ring. A low serum copper level (9.43 µmol/L; reference 10.50-29.90) prompted further evaluation; genetic testing incidentally identified a heterozygous ATP7B variant (NM_000053.4:c.2851 C > T; p.Gln951Ter), reported as likely pathogenic. WD was considered. However, ceruloplasmin was normal (231.6 mg/L; reference 200.0-420.0 mg/L), ceruloplasmin oxidase activity measured by the p-phenylenediamine method was normal (0.372 OD; reference > 0.200 OD), liver biochemistry was normal (ALT 11 U/L, AST 16 U/L, GGT 14 U/L; bilirubin within reference range), and abdominal ultrasound showed a normal liver and biliary tree. Crucially, a follow-up quantitative 24-hour urinary copper test was strictly normal, and parental segregation analysis confirmed that the ATP7B variant represented a paternally inherited heterozygous state without biochemical evidence of Wilson disease, making active Wilson disease highly unlikely. This case illustrates a critical diagnostic pitfall: incidental heterozygous ATP7B variants can trigger severe diagnostic anchoring bias. To prevent overdiagnosis, genetic findings must be subordinated to strict phenotype-driven evaluations, formal Leipzig scoring, and definitive biochemical gold standards.

papers.title: Parental Health Information Needs, Child-Health Literacy, and Use of Generative AI Among Parents of Children Aged 0 to 4 Years in France: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background: The first thousand days are a sensitive window for child health and social health inequalities. When routine care falls short, parents of young children turn to online sources and, recently, to generative artificial intelligence (AI). Evidence on their concerns, child-health literacy, and AI use is scarce. Objective: To describe health informational needs and concerns, child-health literacy, and use of AI for child-health questions, including differences by parental role and parity, among parents of young children. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, two anonymous self-administered online questionnaires were disseminated through a digital health application between May 12 and June 11, 2026, to French-speaking parents of at least one child aged 0 to 47 months in France. Questionnaire 1 covered unmet information needs, concerns across 16 topics, perceived intra-couple concordance, and confidence in routine care. Questionnaire 2 covered a four-item child-health literacy quiz and AI use (frequency, topics, 12-month trend, barriers, trust conditions, perceived effect on consultations, and disclosure). Results: In total, 12,634 parents responded (Questionnaire 1, n=5,410; Questionnaire 2, n=7,224), mostly mothers (94.6% and 92.9%). Most (61.8%) had searched for information without finding a clear, reliable answer, selecting a median of 4 (Interquartile range [IQR] 3-7) over 16 topics. Leading concerns were sleep (51.3%), nutrition (48.1%), and education (i.e., upbringing and behavior) (47.8%). Mothers were nearly twice as likely as fathers to select accident prevention (26.5% vs 16.3%) and parental mental health (38.7% vs 28.6%); first-time parents selected most topics more often than experienced parents, most markedly dental hygiene (43.8% vs 27.6%). The median child-health literacy score was 3 (IQR 3-4) on a 0-to-4 quiz, with 19.9% of parents scoring 2 or below; tooth-brushing age was the weakest item (68.4% correct). Mothers outscored fathers on every item. More than half of parents (54.2%) had used AI for a child-health question, 11.2% weekly; among those reporting a trend, 68.3% had increased AI use for child-health questions over the year and 6.2% decreased it. The main barriers to AI use were a preference for professionals (55.9%) and reliability concerns (48.7%); trust depended most on medical oversight of the tool (76.6%). AI use appeared additive, with 66.8% reporting no change in healthcare visit frequency. One third (35.5%) had told an AI something shared with neither a professional nor their network, rising to 64.1% among regular users. Conclusions: Parental informational needs were widespread and frequently unmet. AI has become a common and fast-rising source for child-health questions, at times a confidential one, used alongside rather than instead of professionals. Child-health literacy was generally high but uneven, with oral health the clearest gap. Strengths include the sample size and early-generative-AI timing; limitations include the cross-sectional design, self-report, digital-recruitment selection bias, and the small proportion of fathers.
